title: Hypothesis Runway: tiered exposure, per-cohort power checks, and auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams need a standardized A/B and canary framework that safely introduces model variants with measurable statistical guarantees. Current ad-hoc rollouts lead to noisy signals, uneven cohort exposure, and manual rollback decisions.

Goal: Deliver a composable experiment control plane ("Hypothesis Runway") that orchestrates tiered exposure schedules, per-cohort power checks, sequential statistical stopping rules, and automated rollback triggers. The feature should integrate with Redwood Console, the Experiments API, and runtime routing so teams can declare hypotheses, cohorts, and rollout policies in one place.

Scope: MVP focuses on model version A/B and canary flows (no multi-armed bandits yet), support for shadow traffic mode, per-route cohort targeting, an early-stop rule based on multi-metric checks, and an autorevert policy that safely demotes a variant and rebalances traffic. Includes observability: per-variant dashboards, cohort-level metrics, and alerting hooks for SREs and product owners.
acceptance_criteria: API: Create/update experiments that accept hypothesis, cohorts, exposure schedule (staged percentages), and stopping criteria.
Console: UI for configuring tiered exposure schedules and visualizing per-cohort sample sizes and power estimates before launch.
Runtime: Traffic router respects scheduled exposure, supports shadow (0% exposure with full metrics collection), and can demote variants automatically on trigger.
Statistical engine: Implements sequential checks (e.g., group-sequential or alpha-spending) with configurable family-wise controls and reports p-values, confidence intervals, and ES estimates.
Auto-rollback: Policy executes within SLA constraints, logs incident, and reassigns traffic back to the baseline with an audit entry.
Observability: Dashboards show per-variant key metrics, sample sizes, conversion rates, latency percentiles, and drift indicators; alert rules for early-stop conditions are configurable.
Docs: Runbook and quickstart for PM/Eng with examples for text-generation latency/cost and quality metrics.
Tests: E2E test covering a canary schedule, statistical stop on quality regression, and automated rollback execution in staging.
Security: Experiment definitions stored with RBAC access; experiment audit trail available via Console and API.
Performance: Experiment orchestration adds <4% p99 request latency overhead in control path; shadow traffic folded to sidecar telemetry path.
technical_notes: Statistical approach: Use alpha-spending with optional Bayes-augmented reporting. Default gate is two-stage group sequential with early-stop for harm at 95% CI and min power 80% for target metric.
Power estimation: Pre-launch simulation based on recent traffic slices; estimate per-cohort min sample size and warn in UI if expected exposure won't reach power within schedule window.
Routing: Implement exposure enforcement in routing plane using tokenized rollout keys and counters, with fallback to baseline on router disconnect.
Shadow traffic: Mirror full requests to variant path; ensure no side-effects on downstream services (idempotency or stubbed writes) and tag telemetry to avoid billing impact.
Auto-rollback safety: Two-step demotion — soft demote (reduce to 0% and mark), then hard demote (remove variant) after confirmation window; supports manual override.
Data pipeline: Metric ingestion must include variant_id and cohort tags; use streaming downsample for high-cardinality metrics to preserve throughput.
Trade-offs: Conservative default thresholds to avoid false rollbacks may delay detection of regressions; allow advanced users to relax thresholds.
Integration points: Experiments API, Console, Runtime router, Metrics pipeline, Alerting (PagerDuty/Slack), Audit log service.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize PRD + design review; secure SRE/Privacy sign-off for shadow path.
Week 1-2: Backend API + statistical engine MVP; simple UI wireframes.
Week 3: Router integration for scheduled exposure and shadow routing; basic metrics tagging.
Week 4: Console UI, power estimator, and simulated experiment runner for validation.
Week 5: Staging E2E tests with synthetic traffic; runbook and on-call rotations for initial launches.
Week 6: Pilot with 2 internal teams (Search and Assistant); collect feedback and harden defaults.
Post-pilot: Iterate on UX, add multi-metric composite gates, and expose advanced configs for Platform customers.
metrics: Primary metric: per-variant quality score (e.g., human-rated utility or automated proxy).
Secondary metrics: latency p95, cost-per-request, error rate, and token usage delta.
Statistical thresholds: default alpha=0.05 two-sided with alpha-spending; default power target 0.8.
Operational SLAs: rollback executed within 60s of trigger; console reflects change within 30s.
Safety caps: max exposure per-step default 20%; absolute exposure ceiling 50% for initial rollouts for new model families.
False positive budget: configurable global cap to limit spurious rollbacks across multiple simultaneous experiments.
